summary.summary: You were in the hospital for a weak heart and lung infection. Your heart was not pumping well and fluid built up in your lungs and legs. You also had a kidney injury that got better. Some of your medicines changed while you were here. The most important thing to do at home is weigh yourself every morning and call your care team if your weight goes up fast.

diagnoses.plain: Weak heart that does not pump well (pump strength was 30%)
Lung infection in the lower right lung
Kidney injury that got better before you went home
Long-term low red blood cell count

new.name: Furosemide
new.why: To remove extra fluid from your body

new.name: Losartan
new.why: To help your heart and lower your blood pressure

new.name: Empagliflozin
new.why: To help your heart and manage your blood sugar

new.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
new.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 3 more days
new.why: To finish treating your lung infection

continue.name: Metoprolol succinate
continue.why: To help your heart beat in a steady, healthy way

continue.name: Apixaban
continue.why: To prevent blood clots because of your irregular heartbeat

continue.name: Atorvastatin
continue.why: To keep your cholesterol at a healthy level

continue.name: Metformin
continue.why: To manage your blood sugar — only if your kidney function stays stable

stop.name: Lisinopril
stop.why: Stopped because your medicine was changed to losartan

stop.name: Spironolactone
stop.why: On hold until your doctor checks your kidney function and potassium level

stop.name: Ibuprofen/other NSAIDs
stop.why: Do not take these pain relievers — they can make heart failure and kidney problems worse

checklist.text: Take furosemide 40 mg every morning — try to take it early in the day
Take losartan 25 mg once a day
Take empagliflozin 10 mg once a day
Finish all 3 remaining days of amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice a day — even if you feel better
checklist.due: twice a day for 3 more days

checklist.text: Weigh yourself at the same time every morning and write it down
Write down any new symptoms each day along with your weight
Get a basic metabolic panel blood test to check your kidneys and potassium
checklist.due: before or at your first follow-up visit within 1 week

checklist.text: See your primary care doctor for a follow-up visit
See your heart doctor (cardiologist) for a follow-up visit
Eat a low-salt diet — aim for no more than 2 grams of sodium a day
Follow the fluid limits your heart-failure team gave you
Do not take ibuprofen or any other NSAIDs (anti-inflammatory pain relievers) unless your doctor says it is okay

goToER: New or worsening shortness of breath, especially at rest
Legs or belly swelling up fast
callClinic: Your weight goes up quickly — follow the weight plan your heart-failure team gave you
Fever or cough gets worse even while taking antibiotics
You notice signs of unusual bleeding (because you take apixaban, a blood thinner)

followUps.why: To check how you are doing after leaving the hospital
To review your heart function and adjust your heart medicines

followUps.who: Heart-failure team or primary care doctor
followUps.why: To review your blood test results for kidney function and potassium, and decide about restarting spironolactone

questionsToAsk: At what number on the scale should I call the clinic about a weight gain?
When will you decide if it is safe to restart spironolactone?
Are there any pain relievers I can safely use instead of ibuprofen?
What signs of bleeding should I watch for while taking apixaban?
How will you know if my kidney function is stable enough to keep taking metformin?

translation.summary: Usted estuvo en el hospital por un corazón débil y una infección en los pulmones. Su corazón no bombeaba bien y se acumuló líquido en sus pulmones y piernas. También tuvo una lesión en los riñones que mejoró. Algunos de sus medicamentos cambiaron mientras estuvo aquí. Lo más importante que debe hacer en casa es pesarse cada mañana y llamar a su equipo de salud si su peso sube rápido.

new.name: Furosemide
new.howOften: una vez al día por la boca
new.why: Para eliminar el exceso de líquido de su cuerpo

new.name: Losartan
new.howOften: una vez al día por la boca
new.why: Para ayudar a su corazón y bajar su presión arterial

new.name: Empagliflozin
new.howOften: una vez al día por la boca
new.why: Para ayudar a su corazón y controlar su azúcar en la sangre

new.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
new.howOften: dos veces al día por la boca durante 3 días más
new.why: Para terminar de tratar su infección pulmonar

continue.name: Metoprolol succinate
continue.why: Para ayudar a que su corazón lata de manera estable y saludable

continue.name: Apixaban
continue.why: Para prevenir coágulos de sangre debido a su latido irregular del corazón

continue.name: Atorvastatin
continue.why: Para mantener su colesterol en un nivel saludable

continue.name: Metformin
continue.why: Para controlar su azúcar en la sangre — solo si la función de sus riñones se mantiene estable

stop.name: Lisinopril
stop.why: Se suspendió porque su medicamento fue cambiado a losartan

stop.name: Spironolactone
stop.why: En pausa hasta que su médico revise la función de sus riñones y su nivel de potasio

stop.name: Ibuprofen/other NSAIDs
stop.why: No tome estos analgésicos — pueden empeorar la insuficiencia cardíaca y los problemas de riñón
